title: "GM Session Guide: Chapter 4 (The God's Demand)"
subtitle: "GM guide — Chapter 4"
---

*Vercingetorix named the cult before he was put down at the fort in Session 3. The party now knows what they're looking for: a hidden dungeon in the forest where two of his own chieftains have spent months feeding something they believe is Mars. This session is that dungeon, start to finish.*

**Level:** 5 (marsh) &rarr; 6 (rest of dungeon) &rarr; Advance to 7 at session end · **Players:** 6 (Iris, Julia Jana, Tanit, Rivia, Ursula, Brian) · **Time:** 4-5 hrs · **Type:** Dungeon crawl

---

<div class="session-tree">

<details open>
<summary>📋 Session Quick-Reference — The Whole Session in One Page</summary>

| | |
|---|---|
| **Central question** | What does devotion to a starving god actually produce, once it succeeds? |
| **What must happen** | (1) The party crosses the marsh and clears the Blood Cult Dungeon, room by room. (2) They reach the Core Room and learn what the crystal-star focus actually is and what destroying it will cost. |
| **Player goal** | Cross the marsh, clear the dungeon, defeat the Glabrezu, and learn the shape of Session 5's cost. |
| **Real stakes** | Whether the party recognizes the chieftains' fate as tragedy rather than just another fight. Whether they learn enough in the Core Room to walk into Session 5 prepared rather than surprised. |
| **Session peak moment** | The Gathering Hall: the two chieftains, now Wraiths, turn to face the party in silence for one full round before the fight starts. |
| **Closing image** | The crystal-star focus, examined but unbroken, absorbing every blow thrown at it. The party now knows the name of the place they need to go next. |

**NPCs active this session:**

| NPC | Location at session start | Wants | Role this session |

**What is NOT in this session:** the old six-day fort siege (Berserkers, Cultist of Mars fanatics, Tribal Warriors, Animated Armor, Quintus Flavius, a tunnel escort to an antechamber). None of that survives in the campaign's actual structure -- see `CAMPAIGN_LOG.md` and `SCRUM_BACKLOG.md`'s Epic 8 for why.

<details>
<summary>🎬 Scene 0: The Marsh</summary>

Load `SkeletonFortressEntrancePublic.jpg`.

> *The trees thin out and the ground goes soft underfoot before you see why. Ahead, the hillside opens in a mouth -- not a metaphor. A skull carved from the living rock, easily twenty feet across, its eye sockets black even at midday. A causeway of bone and old skulls runs from between its teeth down into a wide, glowing green marsh that splits around the path like water around a stone. The light doesn't flicker like fire. It breathes, slow, the way something alive breathes.*

The bone causeway is the only dry footing. Leaving it means wading through glowing green water.

**Marsh hazard (each round off the causeway):** DC 12 Constitution save or one level of exhaustion and 1 point of temporary corruption. The causeway itself is always safe.

**Two supply caches** at the marsh's near corners. DC 11 Wisdom (Investigation) turns up rations gone green with the same glow, a tally-marked stick counting days, and -- second cache -- a torn strip of cloth matching the two chieftains' warband colors. Third and final confirmation this is the right place.

**Encounter:** 2 **Banshees** rise from the marsh as the party crosses -- early followers who didn't survive tending this place. They rise mid-causeway, roughly a third of the way across, not on arrival. Stagger their Wails; never let both go off in the same round.

</details>

<details>
<summary>🎬 Scene 1: The Ossuary</summary>

Load `Blood-Cult-Dungeon-Gridded-29x43-MapPublic.jpg`, west skull room.

> *The room ahead is round, and its far wall is shaped like the thing you just walked through -- another skull, smaller, teeth picked out in inlaid bone. The floor is a carpet of femurs and ribs, stacked with a care that took someone a long time.*

DC 13 Intelligence (History) (active): the bones are sorted by size, by age, deliberately -- curated for months, not years. Matches the marsh tally-stick.

**Encounter:** 2 **Bone Nagas**, coiled among the bones. They wait until a character disturbs the bone floor or casts a spell before acting. Use their spellcasting to control -- Hold Person on the party's main damage dealer, Ray of Enfeeblement on a melee striker.

</details>

<details>
<summary>🎬 Scene 2: The Blood-Growth Rooms</summary>

Same map, east rooms.

> *The stone here has stopped being stone. Something has grown over it -- clusters of dark red matter, wet-looking, veined, thick as a fist in places and swollen tight. They shift, very slightly, when you get close. Not with the room's air currents.*

DC 12 Wisdom (Medicine) or Intelligence (Nature) (active): organic, fed on blood deliberately and repeatedly, over a long period.

**Encounter:** a **Yochlol**, hidden in the growths in spider form, supported by 2 **Dretches**. The Yochlol drops once the party investigates the growths; the Dretches emerge a round later, framed as the room "reacting." Insect Plague is available if the fight runs long -- the growths are already a breeding ground.

</details>

<details>
<summary>🎬 Scene 3: The Minor Altar</summary>

Same map, center room.

> *Four pillars ring a low dais at the room's center, and the dais itself pulses -- not light exactly, more like a heartbeat you can see. This isn't the room you came here looking for. It feels like a rehearsal for one.*

DC 14 Intelligence (Religion) (active): this altar never completed a working -- every mark is a false start. Whatever the cult built up to happened elsewhere.

**Encounter:** 2 **Shadow Demons**, using the four pillars to break line of sight constantly. On sight, but they immediately vanish between pillars rather than engaging directly -- striking from a different pillar each round. Being stalked, not a fair fight.

</details>

<details>
<summary>🎬 Scene 4: The Rune Lock</summary>

Same map, south of center.

> *Four tiles are set into the floor here, each etched with a different symbol, each lit from beneath in a different color -- cyan, green, magenta, yellow. There's no door ahead. Whatever this room is guarding, it's guarding it by making you choose.*

**Solution:** cyan &rarr; green &rarr; yellow &rarr; magenta ("beginning, growth, harvest, blood" -- the cult's own private liturgy). DC 13 Intelligence (Investigation) or Wisdom (Insight) on wear patterns hints at the order.

**Failure:** DC 12 Dexterity save or 2d6 force damage, sequence resets. No lockout, ever -- this room should never be a hard stop.

This is the session's breather beat. If pacing needs it, one fled Dretch from Scene 2 can ambush from hiding -- don't force it otherwise.

</details>

<details>
<summary>🎬 Scene 5: The Gathering Hall</summary>

Same map, south end.

> *This room was built to hold people. Rows of worn stone mark where dozens once knelt, facing a long table at the far end, still laid with offerings gone black with age. Whatever congregation gathered here, it hasn't gathered in some time. But something is still standing at that table.*

**The reveal:** what's still standing are the two cult chieftains, or what's left of them. DC 13 Wisdom (Insight) or Intelligence (Investigation) before combat identifies torn fragments matching the marsh cache's warband colors.

**Encounter:** 3 **Wraiths** -- the two chieftains and one devoted follower.

**This room needs to land as tragedy, not just a fight.** The chieftains got exactly what they thought they wanted, and it consumed them entirely. Play their first actions as recognition, not aggression: they turn toward the party slowly and, for one round, do nothing but watch. If spoken to directly, one fragmentary sentence each ("we asked --" / "it heard us") before the hunger takes back over.

**Escalation:** Create Specter from any humanoid corpse killed in the last minute within 10 ft. Cap total specters at 3 for table sanity. Stagger it the same way the Banshees' Wails were staggered in Scene 0.

</details>

<details>
<summary>🎬 Scene 6: The Core Room</summary>

Load `CastleCoreRoomPublic.jpg`.

> *The stair curves up into a perfectly circular chamber. Four stone faces watch from the walls at the compass points -- not gods, not ancestors, just teeth and eyes carved to be looked at from every angle at once. At the center, on a low dais, a crystal the shape of a broken star burns steady and cold. It is the only thing in this entire dungeon that looks cared for.*

**What the crystal actually is:** DC 15 Intelligence (Arcana) or Intelligence (Religion) (active, or automatic once the party knows what Vercingetorix revealed): this is the cult's real altar and the marsh's real source. Every drop of blood spent in every room below was tribute funneled here -- not to summon Mars, but to keep something that answers to his name fed and present a little longer. The rooms below weren't separate encounters. They were all one working, and this was always where it was going.

**The guardian:** a **Glabrezu**, bound to the focus, not merely standing near it. It opens with Darkness centered on the dais, then uses Confusion and Power Word Stun to isolate whoever gets closest to the crystal. It will not chase a fleeing party far -- its purpose is guarding the focus, not hunting.

**The actual payoff of this session:** once the Glabrezu is dealt with, the crystal can be examined but not destroyed here -- trying visibly fails, absorbing whatever is thrown at it. That's Session 5's job. This scene should end with the party knowing the name of the place they need to go next and the shape of the cost waiting there -- not with the spear's story resolved.

**Advance to Level 7.**

</details>

<details>
<summary>🏛️ DM Notes</summary>

**OGAS this session:**

- **The two chieftains (now Wraiths):** Objective: feed the war-god who could finally give their people victories that lasted. Goal (this session): none anymore. Agenda: guard the hall they built, unable to leave or stop. Secret: they were not lied to about Mars's hunger -- they were right about what he wanted, and wrong about what answering it would cost them personally.
- **Tribune Lucius:** unchanged objective from Session 3 -- this must never reach Rome. This dungeon confirms everything he already suspected about the spear. Covers the party's retreat if the Core Room fight goes badly; does not touch the crystal himself.

**Session 4 &rarr; Session 5 handoff -- write these down now:**

| Question | Session 5 implication |
|---|---|
| Did the party learn what the crystal requires to be destroyed? | Determines how prepared they are walking into Session 5 |
| Are all three Wraiths accounted for? | An escaped Wraith is a loose thread worth resolving in Session 5 |
| What is each character's corruption level after this session? | Proximity to the focus should have pushed at least one up -- note who |
| Is Lucius still with the party? | Carries forward into Session 5 unchanged unless this session broke that |

</details>
